notes: Omaha, NEBRASKA — Douglas County seat, the state's largest city (pop. ~486k, 148.9 sq mi). 152,255 shipped parcels, $7.77B land value / $58.51B total assessed value. Source: Douglas County / City of Omaha GIS (DOGIS) parcel layer dcgis.org/server/rest/services/vector/Cityworks_Parcels_DCHD/FeatureServer/0 (217,384 countywide rows: geometry + the Assessor's LAND_VALUE / IMPROVEMEN / TOTAL_VALU + CLASS + DCAACCTYPE + CONDO flag + BLDG_DESC + SQ_FEET), clipped by representative point to the City Limits layer (Hosted/City_Limits_(source)_view, town='Omaha'). See run_omaha.py.

WHY THAT LAYER: dcgis.org's `vector/Parcels_public` is the same 217,384 polygons with NO value fields at all, and `vector/Parcels` needs a token. The 'Cityworks' parcel layers (CCSM / DCHD / PRPP / EQC — one layer republished under four names for the City's work-order system) are the ones carrying the Assessor's values. Owner-name fields are never requested.

VALUES ARE 100% OF ACTUAL VALUE. Nebraska assesses residential and commercial property at 100% of actual (market) value (Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-201(1)); the median Omaha house is $247k total, land $22.9k. Agricultural land is assessed at 75% (77-201(2)), but only 72 shipped parcels are agricultural, so it is documented rather than grossed up. TOTAL = LAND + IMPROVEMENT on every parcel.

EXEMPT (dropped): CLASS E (Ex Government / Religious / Charitable / Educational / Cemetery) and CLASS U / 'State Assd' railroad, pipeline and public-utility property (valued centrally by the State; the county carries it at $0). 5,629 footprints dropped; their combined county land value is $37,200, i.e. Douglas County zeroes exempt property, so nothing taxable is lost. 'Par Ex' (partially exempt) and 'Govt Lse' (taxable leasehold) accounts carry assessed value and ship.

STACKED FOOTPRINTS ARE SUMMED (playbook §5, skill §2a). Douglas County draws every CONDO UNIT as the whole development's lot polygon — up to 405 identical polygons on one tower — each carrying that unit's land + improvement value; and every Omaha TIF ('OMAHA REDEVELOPMENT') parcel is split into a base PIN and a TIF-excess PIN on one identical polygon with different values. Both are distinct value records on one footprint, so identical (and >=95%-overlapping) footprints collapse to one parcel with the values SUMMED: 9,611 records -> 1,988 footprints (254 condo developments, 1,772 TIF parcels). The 5 multi-polygon PINs are the opposite case (one value broadcast) and take first + union. Post-flight asserts shipped land == the taxable roll's land to the dollar. `value_records` and `tif_parcel` are in the popup.

CONDO LAND IS THE ASSESSOR'S OWN SPLIT: condo units carry ~3% of their value as land (vs ~10% for houses), so summed condo developments read somewhat low on land (median $3.80/sqft, about the citywide median). Published as-is, not imputed.

TOWNHOME FOOTPRINT LOTS (skill §6a/§6b): 7 newer subdivisions (e.g. Villages on Sprague: 129 lots of 528 sqft at $10,000 land each, plus $100 HOA outlots) plat each townhouse as a building-footprint lot. Those merge down onto their subdivision's outlots under a plat-dominance gate (footprint lots >= 60% of the subdivision's valued parcels): 250 lots + 10 outlots -> 7 developments, land $/sqft p50 $18.95 -> $7.12. Rowhouse subdivisions with NO outlot (Rows at SoMa, Dahlman Rows, 31 Mason ...) are genuine fee-simple lots and stay individual, as do ~530 other footprint-sized lots; they render hot but bounded (p99 $12/sqft citywide).

One assessor anomaly ships as-is: PIN 1021740129, a 1,605 sqft lot carrying $342,200 of land ($213/sqft, the city max) in a small-lot subdivision — the assessor's own number (Seattle Westlake / Hartford '0 OLIVE ST' precedent).

LAND IS CHEAP IN THE ASSESSOR'S BOOKS: citywide median $2.87/sqft (single-family lot median 8,125 sqft, land ~10% of value). Downtown (within ~600 m of 16th & Farnam) runs ~$27/sqft area-weighted and the Old Market ~$24, vs ~$5-6.5 in Dundee / Aksarben / Midtown, ~$3 in Millard and ~$1.3 in North Omaha around 30th & Ames.

PARKING: OSM-only and UNCLASSIFIED (--osm-only --no-classify): 2,129 lots / 1,530 acres / ~$460M estimated land value, 5.9% of the city's taxable land value. Within ~1 km of 16th & Farnam, 117 lots cover ~50 acres (~19% of taxable parcel acreage downtown). The surface-vs-structure classifier's Overpass grid fetch hung twice (overpass-api.de and the maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-10-12, while the Lincoln run was hitting Overpass concurrently); re-run without --no-classify when Overpass is quiet. Lots on exempt land (UNMC, Creighton, Eppley Airfield, schools, churches) are clipped out with the exempt parcels. The assessor itself codes only 4 parcels as 'Parking Lot', so OSM is the only parking signal; OSM undercounts outside well-mapped areas.
Baked to PMTiles + H3 (152k parcels; H3 ladder r7/r8/r10/r11, hexes z0-11, parcels z12+) with --drop-remnants to match hideRemnants (115 sub-500-sqft slivers).
